title: GitHub Actions
label: GHA
desc: Automate builds, tests and deploys with workflows that run on GitHub's runners.

sections.title: Setup
sections.description: Authenticate the CLI, check the token scopes and list what runs in the repository.

snippets.code:
# Log in against github.com; the web flow stores a token for the CLI
gh auth login --hostname github.com --git-protocol ssh --web

# Confirm which account is active and which scopes the token carries
gh auth status

# Every workflow file GitHub found, including disabled ones
gh workflow list --all

# The last ten runs of the current repository
gh run list --limit 10

# Follow a run live, then read only the failing step's log
gh run watch
gh run view --log-failed

# Re-run the failed jobs without pushing again
gh run rerun --failed

sections.title: Workflow File
sections.description: One file per pipeline under .github/workflows, with triggers, jobs and steps.

snippets.code:
name: CI

# on holds the triggers; push and pull_request are the common pair
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

# Jobs run in parallel unless they declare needs
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test

# Workflows are only read from this directory at the repository root
ls .github/workflows

# Catch syntax and expression mistakes before pushing
actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml

# Start a manual run of a workflow that declares workflow_dispatch
gh workflow run deploy.yml

sections.title: Triggers
sections.description: Choose what starts a run: pushes, pull requests, schedules or manual dispatch.

snippets.code:
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, release/**]
    paths:
      - "src/**"
      - "Cargo.toml"
    tags: ["v*"]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

on:
  # Five fields, UTC, so 03:30 every weekday
  schedule:
    - cron: "30 3 * * 1-5"

  # Manual runs can carry typed inputs
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: Target environment
        type: choice
        options: [staging, production]
        default: staging
      dry_run:
        type: boolean
        default: false

# One block may hold several triggers; they are OR-ed
on:
  # After another workflow finishes, regardless of success
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [CI]
    types: [completed]

  # On a published release, and on a tag push
  release:
    types: [published]
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

sections.title: Jobs
sections.description: Group steps into jobs, chain them with needs and pass values between them.

snippets.code:
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - id: meta
        run: echo "version=$(git describe --tags --always)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  deploy:
    # Waits for build; outputs are read from the needs context
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    environment: production
    steps:
      - run: echo "Deploying ${{ needs.build.outputs.version }}"

jobs:
  test:
    # GitHub-hosted labels are ubuntu-24.04, macos-14, windows-2022
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

  gpu:
    # Labels set on a self-hosted runner
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux, gpu]

  in-container:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    container:
      image: node:22-bookworm
      options: --cpus 2
    steps:
      - run: node --version

# Top-level: one run per branch, and a new push cancels the running one
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

# Or per job, when only the deploy must not overlap
jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    concurrency:
      group: deploy-production
      cancel-in-progress: false

sections.title: Steps
sections.description: Single units of work: shell commands, actions from the marketplace or your own repo.

snippets.code:
steps:
  - name: Run the tests
    working-directory: ./app
    env:
      RUST_LOG: debug
    run: cargo test --all-features

  # A step can take several commands; the shell is bash on Linux and macOS
  - name: Build the front end
    shell: bash
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      npm ci
      npm run build

steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    with:
      fetch-depth: 0

  - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
    with:
      python-version: "3.13"

  - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
    with:
      context: .
      push: false
      tags: cheatrs-api:ci

steps:
  - id: check
    run: echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  # Runs only when the previous step reported a change
  - if: steps.check.outputs.changed == 'true'
    run: ./scripts/deploy.sh

  # A failing step does not stop the job, but the job still fails at the end
  - continue-on-error: true
    run: ./scripts/flaky-report.sh

sections.title: Matrix
sections.description: Run one job many times over a set of values, with additions and exclusions.

snippets.code:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-24.04, macos-14]
        node: [20, 22]
        exclude:
          - os: macos-14
            node: 20
        include:
          # Adds a third variable to existing combinations only
          - node: 22
            coverage: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
      - run: npm test

jobs:
  list:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      targets: ${{ steps.set.outputs.targets }}
    steps:
      - id: set
        run: echo 'targets=["api","worker"]' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  build:
    needs: list
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      matrix:
        # Reads a JSON array produced by the previous job
        target: ${{ fromJSON(needs.list.outputs.targets) }}
    steps:
      - run: echo "Building ${{ matrix.target }}"

sections.title: Secrets and Env
sections.description: Pass credentials and configuration without writing them into the repository.

snippets.code:
env:
  APP_ENV: production

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    env:
      # Repository or organization secret; never available in forks
      API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.API_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - env:
          STEP_ONLY: value
        run: ./scripts/deploy.sh

      # Secrets are masked in logs but not in files you upload
      - run: echo "${{ secrets.API_TOKEN }}" | docker login ghcr.io -u felipe --password-stdin

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      # GITHUB_TOKEN is minted per run and expires with it
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Built-in variables are already in the environment
      - run: |
          echo "commit $GITHUB_SHA on $GITHUB_REF"
          echo "run $GITHUB_RUN_ID attempt $GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT"

# Store a secret, then read back only the name and update time
gh secret set API_TOKEN --body "$(op read op://ci/api/token)"
gh secret list

# Environment secrets are scoped to a deployment target
gh secret set DB_URL --env production --body "postgres://db.internal/app"

# Repository variables are plain config, visible in the UI
gh variable set REGISTRY --body ghcr.io/felipe

sections.title: Caching
sections.description: Reuse downloaded dependencies between runs; keys decide when a cache is valid.

snippets.code:
steps:
  - uses: actions/cache@v4
    with:
      path: |
        ~/.cargo/registry
        ~/.cargo/git
        target
      # Busted whenever the lockfile changes
      key: cargo-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}
      restore-keys: |
        cargo-${{ runner.os }}-

steps:
  # setup-node handles the cache directory and the key for you
  - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    with:
      node-version: 22
      cache: npm

  - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
    with:
      python-version: "3.13"
      cache: pip
      cache-dependency-path: requirements*.txt

steps:
  - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

  # Layer cache lives in the Actions cache backend, no registry needed
  - uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
    with:
      context: .
      push: true
      tags: ghcr.io/felipe/cheatrs-api:latest
      cache-from: type=gha
      cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

sections.title: Artifacts
sections.description: Keep files produced by a job and hand them to later jobs or to the run page.

snippets.code:
steps:
  - run: npm run build

  # v4 requires a distinct name per job; files are zipped on upload
  - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
    with:
      name: dist
      path: dist/
      retention-days: 7
      if-no-files-found: error

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: coverage
          path: coverage/lcov.info

  report:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: coverage
          path: coverage
      - run: npx codecov --file coverage/lcov.info

# List artifacts of the newest run
gh run view --json artifacts

# Download one artifact of a specific run into a folder
gh run download 1234567890 -n dist -D ./dist

sections.title: Services
sections.description: Run databases and brokers as sidecar containers next to the job.

snippets.code:
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: app
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: app
          POSTGRES_DB: app_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        # The job waits for this to pass before running steps
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U app"
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    steps:
      - run: psql "postgres://app:app@localhost:5432/app_test" -c "select 1"

services:
  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    ports:
      - 6379:6379
    options: >-
      --health-cmd "redis-cli ping"
      --health-interval 5s
      --health-retries 10

steps:
  - run: redis-cli -h localhost -p 6379 ping

  # Containers on the job network are reachable by service name too
  - run: curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/health

sections.title: Conditions
sections.description: Gate jobs and steps with expressions over events, branches and previous results.

snippets.code:
steps:
  - id: tests
    run: npm test

  # Runs only on pushes to main
  - if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push'
    run: ./scripts/deploy.sh

  # Always runs, even after a failure, for cleanup and reports
  - if: always()
    run: ./scripts/upload-report.sh

  # Skips when nothing failed so far
  - if: success()
    run: ./scripts/next.sh

jobs:
  preview:
    # Label check on pull requests; quotes keep the expression a string
    if: >
      github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
      contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'deploy-preview')
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - run: echo "preview for ${{ github.head_ref }}"

sections.title: Permissions
sections.description: Scope GITHUB_TOKEN per workflow or job; anything not listed is denied.

snippets.code:
# Workflow default: read the code, write packages
permissions:
  contents: read
  packages: write

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # Job level replaces, not merges, the workflow default
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | docker login ghcr.io -u "${{ github.actor }}" --password-stdin

# Deny everything, then grant the minimum per job
permissions: {}

jobs:
  comment:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            await github.rest.issues.createComment({
              ...context.repo,
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              body: "Checks finished."
            })

# What the default token can do in this repository
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo} --jq '.permissions'

# Change the repository-wide default to read-only
gh api -X PUT repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/permissions/workflow   -f default_workflow_permissions=read

sections.title: Reusable Workflows
sections.description: Call one workflow from another, with typed inputs and explicit secret passing.

snippets.code:
# .github/workflows/test.yml — the callee
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      node_version:
        type: string
        default: "22"
    secrets:
      npm_token:
        required: false
    outputs:
      status:
        value: ${{ jobs.test.outputs.status }}

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      status: ${{ steps.run.outputs.status }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node_version }}
      - id: run
        run: |
          npm ci && npm test
          echo "status=passed" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

jobs:
  unit:
    # Local path, or owner/repo/.github/workflows/file.yml@v1
    uses: ./.github/workflows/test.yml
    with:
      node_version: "20"
    secrets:
      npm_token: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}

  e2e:
    needs: unit
    uses: felipe/ci-workflows/.github/workflows/e2e.yml@v2
    # Forwards every secret of the caller
    secrets: inherit
    with:
      browser: chromium

sections.title: Common Errors
sections.description: The failures that show up most often, and the setting that actually fixes each one.

snippets.code:
# Symptom: "Resource not accessible by integration" when the job tries to write
# Cause: the default token is read-only on new repositories
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

# Symptom: artifact upload fails with "Conflict: an artifact with this name already exists"
# Cause: v4 needs a unique name per job, and v3 is shut down
- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  with:
    name: coverage-${{ matrix.node }}
    path: coverage/

# Symptom: the workflow never starts
# Cause: the file is not under .github/workflows, or a branch/path filter excludes it
git ls-files .github/workflows
gh workflow list --all

# Symptom: "Bad credentials" on checkout
# Cause: the token lacks contents:read, or a fork PR cannot read secrets
gh auth status
